topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and pedagogical objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, mutation sources, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how intrinsic mutational processes and environmental exposures interact to determine cancer risk across populations.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious pathogens contribute to cancer development, illustrated through the mechanism and epidemiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and chemical agents undergo metabolic processing to form DNA adducts and induce mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and the two-stage model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis where promoters drive clonal expansion and chronic inflammation following initiation.

topics.label: Host susceptibility factors and carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how developmental timing and physiological states influence susceptibility to carcinogens alongside a synthesis of the mechanisms discussed.

topics.label: Methodologies for evaluating carcinogenicity and risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methods used to determine carcinogenicity and assess exposure risks.

topics.label: Conclusion and lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic delivers the closing summary and final concluding remarks for the lecture.
